paper_title: AIForge-Doc: A Benchmark for Detecting AI-Forged Tampering in Financial and Form Documents
authors_year_venue: Jiaqi Wu, Yuchen Zhou, Muduo Xu et al. (2026), arXiv preprint
access_level: abstract (seed; deep read by other sub-agent)
research_problem: Diffusion-API inpainting forgeries of numeric fields in financial/form documents; pixel-level localization benchmark
datasets: AIForge-Doc v1 (4,061 forged images from CORD, WildReceipt, SROIE, XFUND; Gemini 2.5 Flash Image + Ideogram V2 Edit)
image_processing_techniques: Dataset paper; evaluated detectors use RGB + noise-residual (TruFor Noiseprint++) and DCT (DocTamper/DTD)
model_architecture: Benchmark of TruFor, DocTamper (DTD), zero-shot GPT-4o judge
main_contribution: First document benchmark dedicated to AI-inpainting forgeries with DocTamper-compatible masks
reported_results: TruFor AUC 0.751 (vs 0.96 on NIST16); DocTamper AUC 0.563 (vs 0.98 in-dist.), pixel IoU 0.020; GPT-4o AUC 0.509 (abstract)
main_limitations: Only two commercial inpainting APIs; numeric-field edits only; small size; no human study
relevance_to_our_research: Primary dataset. Gap A (no splice/JPEG artifact), Gap B (two generators only -> cross-generator test), Gap C (tiny numeric regions), Gap D (mask quality unknown)
remaining_research_questions: Are masks tight to edited glyphs? Does fine-tuning DTD/TruFor on v1 transfer to v2 (GPT-Image-2)?

paper_title: When the Forger Is the Judge: GPT-Image-2 Cannot Recognize Its Own Faked Documents
authors_year_venue: Jiaqi Wu, Yuchen Zhou, Dennis Tsang Ng et al. (2026), arXiv preprint
research_problem: Can humans, generic/document forensics, or the generator itself detect GPT-Image-2 document forgeries?
datasets: AIForge-Doc v2 (3,066 paired GPT-Image-2 forgeries, pixel masks); human 2AFC study N=120
image_processing_techniques: Benchmark; TruFor (noise residual) and DocTamper (DCT) as detectors
main_contribution: Shows near-chance human and self-judge performance on a single-generator paired dataset
reported_results: Human 2AFC acc 0.501; TruFor 0.599, DocTamper 0.585, self-judge 0.532 (AUC never >0.59) (abstract)
main_limitations: Single generator; detectors zero-shot only (no fine-tuning); paired design may not reflect deployment
relevance_to_our_research: Gap B (v1 vs v2 generator shift = natural cross-generator protocol); Gap D (evaluation protocol design)
remaining_research_questions: Does training on v1 (Gemini/Ideogram) generalize to v2 (GPT-Image-2)?
license: CC-BY-4.0 mentioned in text (UNVERIFIED for dataset)

paper_title: DOCFORGE-BENCH: A Comprehensive 0-shot Benchmark for Document Forgery Detection and Analysis
authors_year_venue: Zengqi Zhao, Weidi Xia, En Wei et al. (2026), arXiv preprint
research_problem: Zero-shot (no fine-tune) evaluation of 14 forgery localizers across 8 document datasets
datasets: DocTamper, T-SROIE, RTM, Tampered-IC13, Receipt (Find-it), FantasyID, MixTamper, FSTS-1.5k
image_processing_techniques: Benchmark; covers RGB, DCT (DTD, FFDN, ADCD-Net), noise-residual methods
model_architecture: 14 pretrained detectors incl. TruFor, CAT-Net, Mesorch, DTD, FFDN, CAFTB-Net
main_contribution: Identifies AUC–F1 calibration gap: tampered pixels are 0.27–4.17% of image, tau=0.5 is miscalibrated; Oracle-F1 2–10x fixed-F1
reported_results: Methods reach Pixel-AUC >=0.76 yet near-zero Pixel-F1; 10-image threshold adaptation recovers 39–55% of Oracle-F1 gap (abstract)
main_limitations: Zero-shot only; no AI-inpainting document set beyond listed; threshold study small
relevance_to_our_research: Gap C (small-region prevalence quantified), Gap D (metric/threshold reliability) — directly motivates threshold-aware evaluation
remaining_research_questions: Does calibration failure persist after fine-tuning on AIForge-Doc? Best small-region metric?

paper_title: Towards Robust Tampered Text Detection in Document Image: New Dataset and New Solution
authors_year_venue: Chenfan Qu, Chongyu Liu, Yuliang Liu et al. (2023), CVPR 2023
research_problem: Visually consistent tampered text localization in photographed/scanned documents
datasets: DocTamper (170k images; test sets DocTamper-Test, FCD, SCD)
image_processing_techniques: JPEG DCT coefficients + quantization table via Frequency Perception Head (FPH); curriculum on JPEG quality
model_architecture: DTD: dual-stream (RGB ConvNeXt + DCT Swin-V2) with Multi-view Iterative Decoder; Curriculum Learning for Tampering Detection (CLTD)
main_contribution: First large-scale document tampering dataset + frequency-aware detector robust to compression
reported_results: +9.2% / +26.3% / +12.3% F-measure over prior SOTA on DocTamper test / FCD / SCD (abstract)
main_limitations: Synthetic (programmatic) tampering; DCT branch assumes JPEG grid alignment; later work shows near-zero zero-shot F1 on other document sets
relevance_to_our_research: Main document baseline. Gap A (DCT dependence), Gap B (synthetic->AI shift), Gap C (robustness to resize/crop)
remaining_research_questions: How does DTD behave when inpainting region is re-encoded as whole image (no double-JPEG trace)?

paper_title: Enhancing Tampered Text Detection Through Frequency Feature Fusion and Decomposition
authors_year_venue: Zhongxi Chen, Shen Chen, Taiping Yao et al. (2024), ECCV 2024 (LNCS 15091)
research_problem: Integrating frequency cues without hurting RGB detection; enhancing small high-frequency tampering traces
datasets: DocTamper (per paper abstract/secondary sources); T-SROIE etc. in later benchmarks
image_processing_techniques: Wavelet-like Frequency Enhancement (WFE) decomposing high/low-frequency; DCT inputs via FPH (REPORTED by DocForge-Bench)
model_architecture: FFDN: ConvNeXt backbone + Visual Enhancement Module (VEM) + WFE, FPN-style head
main_contribution: Frequency fusion/decomposition network for subtle document text tampering
reported_results: not extracted from primary; REPORTED by DocForge-Bench: F1 0.736 on DocTamper, 0.043 on T-SROIE zero-shot
main_limitations: Frequency cues counterproductive for PNG / multiply post-processed images (acknowledged in paper); poor zero-shot transfer (REPORTED)
relevance_to_our_research: Gap A (frequency-artifact reliance), Gap C (small-trace enhancement idea reusable)
remaining_research_questions: Does WFE help on diffusion inpainting where no compression discontinuity exists?

paper_title: ADCD-Net: Robust Document Image Forgery Localization via Adaptive DCT Feature and Hierarchical Content Disentanglement
authors_year_venue: Kahim Wong, Jicheng Zhou, Haiwei Wu et al. (2025), ICCV 2025
research_problem: Robust document forgery localization under resize/crop/JPEG when DCT block grid is misaligned
datasets: DocTamper (+ FCD/SCD), Tianchi real-world forgery set (per references)
image_processing_techniques: Adaptive DCT feature weighting by predicted block-alignment score; RGB/DCT fusion; pristine prototype of background
model_architecture: ADCD-Net: RGB + DCT streams with alignment-score modulation, hierarchical content disentanglement (text vs BG)
main_contribution: Makes DCT cue adaptive -> resilience to distortions; text/background disentanglement
reported_results: Average F1 gain +7.06% from adaptive DCT (text); baseline CAT-Net 0.702 and DTD 0.778 avg F1 quoted in paper
main_limitations: Still synthetic-training; 7x slower than DiffNet (REPORTED by 2606.22285); AI-inpainting not evaluated
relevance_to_our_research: Gap A/C: artifact-adaptive design is a template for AI-forgery case; Gap B untested
remaining_research_questions: Does alignment-score gating degrade gracefully when forgery has no DCT signature at all?

paper_title: Revisiting Tampered Scene Text Detection in the Era of Generative AI
authors_year_venue: Chenfan Qu, Yiwu Zhong, Fengjun Guo et al. (2025), AAAI 2025 (arXiv 2407.21422)
research_problem: Open-set tampered scene text detection: generalize to unseen generative text-editing models

reported_results: Table 5 (OSTF): ours+Cascade-RCNN avg mF 88.62 (seen) vs 75.85 (unseen generators) — drop of ~13 pts (column mapping inferred from table)

paper_title: Toward Real Text Manipulation Detection: New Dataset and New Solution
authors_year_venue: Dongliang Luo, Yuliang Liu et al. (2025), Pattern Recognition (arXiv 2312.06934, 2023)
research_problem: Real (manual) text manipulation detection; synthetic data fails to replicate real tampering attributes
datasets: RTM (14,250 images: 5,986 manual, 5,258 automatic tampered, 3,006 authentic); Tampered-IC13
image_processing_techniques: Multi-modal fusion (RGB + transformed domains e.g. frequency/noise), Consistency-aware Aggregation Hub, Gated Cross Neighborhood-attention Fusion, Tampered-Authentic contrastive learning
model_architecture: Segmentation network with CA Hub + GCNF; evaluated vs RRU-Net, PSCC-Net, CAT-Net v2, MVSS-Net++, DTD
main_contribution: Largest manual tampering dataset; shows SOTA methods falter on real tampering
evaluation_metrics: Pixel-level P/R/F1, image-level AUC; authentic-image stability
reported_results: Tampered-IC13: F1 98.97 vs 96.80 (Wang et al.) (Table 7); on RTM existing methods falter (Table 2, exact columns not extracted)
main_limitations: Non-commercial license; Chinese e-commerce text domain; no generative inpainting
relevance_to_our_research: Gap B (synthetic->real shift analog of AI shift); Gap D (authentic-image false-alarm evaluation)
remaining_research_questions: How much of RTM gain comes from manual tampering diversity vs architecture?

paper_title: TextSleuth: Towards Explainable Tampered Text Detection
authors_year_venue: Chenfan Qu, Jian Liu, Haoxing Chen et al. (2024), arXiv preprint
research_problem: Explainable tampered text detection with natural-language anomaly descriptions
datasets: ETTD (pixel masks + GPT-4o anomaly descriptions); Tampered-IC13; DocTamper subsets
image_processing_techniques: Fused mask prompt; two-stage analysis (coarse-to-fine region zoom)
main_contribution: First explainable tampered-text dataset + LMM baseline; robustness to JPEG/resize reported
evaluation_metrics: Detection accuracy/F1 per domain, OCR accuracy of described text; robustness under JPEG q50/resize
reported_results: Table 3: TextSleuth-7B avg 97.2 vs Qwen2VL-7B 90.7; under JPEG q50 97.2->96.3, resize 0.5 -> 93.0
main_limitations: GPT-4o-generated annotations (annotation bias risk); no pixel IoU reported for LMM; heavy model
relevance_to_our_research: Gap D (auto-annotation bias); Gap C (robustness protocol)
remaining_research_questions: Do LMM explanations hold for numeric-only edits with no visible artifact?

paper_title: DocQT: Improving Document Forgery Localization Robustness via Diverse JPEG Quantization Tables
authors_year_venue: Kylian Ronfleux-Corail, Guillaume Bernard, Mickaël Coustaty et al. (2026), arXiv preprint
research_problem: Train/deploy mismatch of JPEG quantization tables as hidden cause of document localizer failure

paper_title: Efficient Document Tampering Localization with Multi-Level Discrepancy Features and Unified DCT-Quantization Embedding
authors_year_venue: Mohamed Dhouib, Ye Zhu, Sonia Vanier et al. (2026), arXiv preprint

paper_title: Toward Real-world Text Image Forgery Localization: Structured and Interpretable Data Synthesis
authors_year_venue: Zeqin Yu, Haotao Xie, Jian Zhang et al. (2025), arXiv preprint
research_problem: Synthetic-to-real gap in text image forgery localization (T-IFL)
datasets: FSTS synthetic set (from 16,750 logged human tampering instances, 5 types); FSTS-1.5k real test; 5 real test sets

remaining_research_questions: Can FSTS be extended with diffusion-inpainting operators?

main_contribution: Shows dominant forensic signal in AI receipts is arithmetic inconsistency, not visual artifact

paper_title: Can Multi-modal (reasoning) LLMs detect document manipulation?
authors_year_venue: Zisheng Liang, Kidus Zewde, Rudra Pratap Singh et al. (2025), arXiv preprint

model_architecture: GPT-4o/o1, Gemini 2 (thinking), Claude 3.5/3.7, Qwen2.5-VL, Llama, Pixtral, Janus, Grok

paper_title: TextFake: Benchmarking AI-Generated Image Detection on Text-Rich Images
authors_year_venue: Yuning Zhang, Changtao Miao, Mingyu Liao et al. (2026), arXiv preprint
research_problem: AI-generated image detectors on text-rich images (documents, screenshots)
datasets: TextFake (20k images, 28 languages, 4 topics, 2 modalities)
image_processing_techniques: Diagnostics of low-level (frequency/noise) detectors vs text density; distribution-aligned prompting to remove covariate shortcuts
main_contribution: Documents a text-density failure mode of low-level detectors; shortcut-controlled benchmark design
reported_results: Mean accuracy of detectors drops 86.7% (GenImage) -> 51.8% (TextFake); no method >80%; VLM APIs degrade less (GPT-5.4 -18.0%, Claude Sonnet 4.6 -11.3%)

relevance_to_our_research: Gap A (dense glyphs overwhelm low-level cues — directly applies to receipts), Gap B
remaining_research_questions: Does text density also degrade localizers (not just classifiers)?

paper_title: TruFor: Leveraging All-Round Clues for Trustworthy Image Forgery Detection and Localization
authors_year_venue: Fabrizio Guillaro, Davide Cozzolino et al. (2023), CVPR 2023
research_problem: Generalizable forgery detection+localization with confidence map
datasets: Train: PSCC synthetic set; test: Coverage, Columbia, CASIAv1, NIST16, DSO-1, VIPP, OpenForensics, CocoGlide (+ social-media versions)
image_processing_techniques: Noiseprint++ learned noise residual (self-supervised on pristine camera data) fused with RGB
model_architecture: SegFormer-based two-branch encoder, anomaly decoder + confidence decoder + integrity score
main_contribution: Anomaly-vs-pristine-pattern framing; confidence map; robust on social media recompression
evaluation_metrics: Pixel-F1 (best/fixed threshold), image AUC, balanced accuracy
reported_results: Table 1 avg pixel-F1 0.785 (best thr) / 0.696 (fixed); Table 2 avg image AUC 0.857, bAcc 0.781; Facebook/WhatsApp CASIAv1 F1 0.716/0.713 (Table 4)
main_limitations: Camera-fingerprint prior weak for scanned/rendered documents; document AUC 0.751 zero-shot (REPORTED by AIForge-Doc)
relevance_to_our_research: Generic baseline; Gap A (noise residual cue in text-dense scans)
remaining_research_questions: Does Noiseprint++ carry signal in screenshot/scanned receipts without camera noise?

paper_title: Learning JPEG Compression Artifacts for Image Manipulation Detection and Localization
authors_year_venue: Myung-Joon Kwon, Seung-Hun Nam et al. (2022), IJCV (CAT-Net v2; WACV 2021 v1)
research_problem: Localize splicing via JPEG compression artifacts (double compression, grid)

image_processing_techniques: DCT coefficient volume + quantization table input; double-JPEG pretraining; DCT stream
model_architecture: CAT-Net: HRNet RGB stream + DCT stream fusion
main_contribution: Shows CNNs can learn DCT distributions when spatial coordinates are preserved
reported_results: GRIP: 76.45% p-F1 / 91.87% p-AP (vs 10.98% Noiseprint); double-JPEG pretraining raises GRIP p-F1 from 24.60 to 76.45
main_limitations: Fails on non-JPEG or resized/misaligned grids; artifact-specific
relevance_to_our_research: Gap A canonical artifact-dependent baseline; DCT branch reused by DTD/FFDN/ADCD-Net
remaining_research_questions: Does an API re-encode the whole image (single JPEG) and null the cue?

paper_title: MVSS-Net: Multi-View Multi-Scale Supervised Networks for Image Manipulation Detection
authors_year_venue: Chengbo Dong, Xinru Chen, Ruohan Hu et al. (2023), IEEE TPAMI (ICCV 2021 conference version)
research_problem: Learn manipulation-sensitive yet authentic-specific features; low false alarms
datasets: Train CASIAv2 / DEFACTO-84k; test Columbia, Coverage, CASIAv1, NIST16, DEFACTO-12k

main_contribution: Explicit boundary-artifact and noise views; authentic-image supervision for specificity
reported_results: Table 6 Com-F1 0.711 (Columbia), 0.565, 0.317, 0.205 across four test sets (MVSS-Net > FCN baseline)
main_limitations: Boundary-artifact view is a known shortcut for blended edits (see Aoudi 2026, Yermakov 2026)
relevance_to_our_research: Boundary-artifact theme; Gap A (edge shortcut), Gap D (specificity on authentic images)
remaining_research_questions: Do inpainting APIs leave Sobel-detectable seams in small numeric regions?

paper_title: PSCC-Net: Progressive Spatio-Channel Correlation Network for Image Manipulation Detection and Localization
authors_year_venue: Xiaohong Liu, Yaojie Liu, Jun Chen, Xiaoming Liu (2022), IEEE TCSVT

reported_results: Table rows: PSCC-Net 98.2/84.7/82.9/85.5/80.6 (per-dataset values, metric column headers not extracted)

paper_title: IML-ViT: Benchmarking Image Manipulation Localization by Vision Transformer
authors_year_venue: Xiaochen Ma, Bo Du, Zhuohang Jiang et al. (2023), arXiv preprint
research_problem: Pure ViT benchmark for IML: high resolution, multi-scale, edge supervision

reported_results: Protocol 1 (Table 5): IML-ViT avg F1 0.480 vs NCL 0.396; NIST16 F1 0.654 / AUC 0.945 vs TruFor 0.600/0.859 (Table)
